'''Stephen Mann''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://stephenmann.co.uk/|title=Stephen Mann FRS {{!}}|website=stephenmann.co.uk|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref><ref name="Stephen Mann">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/stephen-mann-11886/|title=Stephen Mann|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/public/home.html?url=%252Fapp%253Fservice%253Dexternalpagemethod%2526page%253DIndex%2526method%253Dview%2526&failReason=Error+reason%253A+err_sub_none|title=Who's Who|website=www.ukwhoswho.com|access-date=2016-07-27}}</ref> [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]], (born 1 April 1955) is Professor of [[Chemistry]], co-director of the Max Planck Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Max Planck Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology – An international research centre|url=https://maxplanck-minimalbiology.bristol.ac.uk/|access-date=2021-04-23|website=maxplanck-minimalbiology.bristol.ac.uk}}</ref> director of the Centre for Organized Matter Chemistry,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bristolcomc.co.uk/|title=COMC {{!}} Centre for Organized Matter Chemistry|website=bristolcomc.co.uk|access-date=2016-08-01}}</ref> director of the Centre for Protolife Research,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bristolprotolife.co.uk|title=CPR {{!}} Centre for Protolife Research|website=www.bristolprotolife.co.uk|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref> and was principal of the Bristol Centre for Functional Nanomaterials<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bcfn.bris.ac.uk|title=BCFN {{!}} BCFN|website=www.bristol.ac.uk/physics/functional-nanomaterials/|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref> at the [[University of Bristol]], UK.

== Education ==
Mann was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[Chemistry]] from the [[University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology]] in 1976,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://your.manchester.ac.uk/login-required?bm=-1832870297|title=Login Required - The University of Manchester|website=your.manchester.ac.uk|access-date=2016-07-27}}</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1982 under the supervision of Professor [[Robert Williams (English chemist)|R. J. P. Williams FRS]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oxfordalumnicommunity.org/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912221318/http://oxfordalumnicommunity.org/|archive-date=12 September 2015|title=Oxford Alumni Community|website=Oxford Alumni Community|access-date=2016-07-27}} </ref>

== Career ==
Following his Doctor of Philosophy degree, Mann was elected to a junior research fellowship at [[University of Oxford|Keble College, University of Oxford]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.wiley-vch.de/vch/journals/2089/interviews2001/am_stephen_mann.pdf|title=Wiley Interview Article}}</ref> and then awarded a lectureship at the [[University of Bath]] in 1984<ref name=":0" /> where he was appointed to a full professorship in 1990. He moved to the [[University of Bristol]] in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bris.ac.uk/chemistry/people/stephen-mann/|title=Bristol People}}</ref>

== Research ==
Mann's research is concerned with the chemical synthesis, characterization and emergence of complex forms of organized matter. His research activities include [[biomineralization]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mann|first=Stephen|date=1988-03-10|title=Molecular recognition in biomineralization|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=332|issue=6160|pages=119–124|doi=10.1038/332119a0|bibcode=1988Natur.332..119M|s2cid=4342005}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/biomineralization-9780198508823?q=Biomineralization&lang=en&cc=gb|title=Biomineralization|series=Oxford Chemistry Masters |date=November 2001 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-850882-3 }}</ref> [[biomimetic material]]s chemistry,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mann|first=Stephen|date=1993-10-07|title=Molecular tectonics in biomineralization and biomimetic materials chemistry|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=365|issue=6446|pages=499–505|doi=10.1038/365499a0|bibcode=1993Natur.365..499M|s2cid=4358080}}</ref> synthesis and self-assembly of [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] objects,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Li|first1=Mei|last2=Schnablegger|first2=Heimo|last3=Mann|first3=Stephen|date=1999-11-25|title=Coupled synthesis and self-assembly of nanoparticles to give structures with controlled organization|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=402|issue=6760|pages=393–395|doi=10.1038/46509|issn=0028-0836|bibcode=1999Natur.402..393L|s2cid=4307826}}</ref> functional [[Nanotechnology|nanomaterials]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Davis|first1=Sean A.|last2=Burkett|first2=Sandra L.|last3=Mendelson|first3=Neil H.|last4=Mann|first4=Stephen|date=1997-01-30|title=Bacterial templating of ordered macrostructures in silica and silica-surfactant mesophases|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=385|issue=6615|pages=420–423|doi=10.1038/385420a0|bibcode=1997Natur.385..420D|s2cid=4280267}}</ref> complexity and emergent behaviour in hybrid [[nanostructure]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mann|first=Stephen|date=2009-10-01|title=Self-assembly and transformation of hybrid nano-objects and nanostructures under equilibrium and non-equilibrium conditions|journal=Nature Materials|language=en|volume=8|issue=10|pages=781–792|doi=10.1038/nmat2496|issn=1476-1122|pmid=19734883|bibcode=2009NatMa...8..781M|doi-access=free}}</ref> and solvent-free liquid proteins.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brogan|first1=Alex P. S.|last2=Sharma|first2=Kamendra P.|last3=Perriman|first3=Adam W.|last4=Mann|first4=Stephen|date=2014-10-06|title=Enzyme activity in liquid lipase melts as a step towards solvent-free biology at 150&nbsp;°C|journal=Nature Communications|language=en|volume=5|page=5058|doi=10.1038/ncomms6058|pmid=25284507|bibcode=2014NatCo...5.5058B|doi-access=free|hdl=1983/97dc22fb-5043-4480-863e-58d47e4bd7f1|hdl-access=free}}</ref> His current work is focused on the design and construction of synthetic [[protocell]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tang|first1=T.-Y. Dora|last2=Hak|first2=C. Rohaida Che|last3=Thompson|first3=Alexander J.|last4=Kuimova|first4=Marina K.|last5=Williams|first5=D. S.|last6=Perriman|first6=Adam W.|last7=Mann|first7=Stephen|date=2014-06-01|title=Fatty acid membrane assembly on coacervate microdroplets as a step towards a hybrid protocell model|journal=Nature Chemistry|language=en|volume=6|issue=6|pages=527–533|doi=10.1038/nchem.1921|pmid=24848239|issn=1755-4330|bibcode=2014NatCh...6..527D|s2cid=205292915 |url=https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/files/42032691/NChem_accepted_text_and_Figures.pdf}}</ref> Mann has published over 550 scientific papers with a current [[h-index]] of 125 and over 64,000 citations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?hl=en&user=r8jslMgAAAAJ&view_op=list_works|title=Stephen Mann - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.co.uk|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref> He is listed in the 2014 [[Science Citation Index|Thomson Reuters index]] of world's most influential scientific minds<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sciencewatch.com/sites/sw/files/sw-article/media/worlds-most-influential-scientific-minds-2014.pdf|title=THE WORLD's Most Influential Scientific Minds 2014|date=2014|publisher=Thomas Reuters}}</ref> and in the top 0.01% of cited scientists.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ioannidis|first1=John P. == Awards and honours ==
Mann was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], UK in 2003.<ref name="Stephen Mann"/> Other accolades include:
* [[Corday-Morgan Prize|Corday-Morgan Medal and Prize]], Royal Society of Chemistry, 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|title=RSC Corday-Morgan Prize Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>
* Fellow [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], 1996.
* [[Max Planck Society|Max-Planck Society]]/[[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] Research Award, 1998–2003.
* [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Interdisciplinary Award]], Royal Society of Chemistry, 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/InterdisciplinaryPrize/PreviousWinners.asp|title=RSC Interdisciplinary Prize Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>
* [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Joseph Chatt Lecture and Medal]], Royal Society of Chemistry, 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/JosephChatt/previouswinners.asp|title=Joseph Chatt Award Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>
* [[de Gennes Prize]] and Medal, Royal Society of Chemistry, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/deGennesPrize/previouswinners.asp|title=de Gennes Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>
* French-British Prize, [[Société chimique de France|Chemical Society of France]], 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2011/7795.html|title=University of Bristol News|date=2011|website=University of Bristol News|publisher=University of Bristol}}</ref>
* [[Davy Medal|Royal Society Davy Medal]] (2016).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/davy-medal/|title=Davy Medal|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>
*Member of Academia Europaea (2020).
